name: workflow_interview
title: A module ask is interviewed, then drafted as "Your workflow" in the person's words

steps.remove_module: Car Wash Site Screener — Austin, gates-first

steps.say: I want help picking car wash sites to open
steps.reply:
I asked you directly since the signal was mixed: **you deleted the Austin car wash screener module right before re-asking this**, which could mean "start over" or could just be tidying up while the underlying work still stands.

For context on what already exists: M0 (single-address gate screen) and M1 (full Travis County parcel screen — zoning, traffic, and competitor gates, all backed by live public data: Austin zoning GIS, TxDOT AADT via Travis County GIS, Texas Comptroller NAICS-811192 permit holders) were built and verified. Only M2 (revenue ranges for passing sites) was left unfinished,

steps.say: It's for me, to decide which sites to pursue and brief my investors. Sites come from brokers by email. Today I check households within 3 miles, density, drive-time population, the traffic on the road and at the main intersection, then I score fourteen things like visibility and access from 1 to 10 with a note each, and write a memo to investors. Thresholds: 45,000 households, 30,000 cars a day. Start with Austin. Go ahead and write it up.
steps.reply:
I pulled together everything from the earlier gates-first build (zoning, traffic, competitor density — all proven live for Austin/Travis County) plus what's new in what you just described — household/drive-time catchment against your 45,000-household bar, intersection-level traffic against your 30,000-cars/day bar, the 14-factor scorecard, and the investor memo — and kicked off a research pass to find real public-data sources for the new pieces and propose the full build as a plan. It takes a few minutes and you'll see the plan card here when it's ready; you can stop it any time.

One thing I

steps.say: Add a minimum lot size of 0.8 acres as one of the checks.
steps.reply:
Added the 0.8-acre minimum lot size as a check, sourced from each parcel's TCAD acreage — the same data the gates already use. It's baked into the page from the start (so it fails a site and shows the actual acreage), alongside everything else: the zoning/traffic/competitor gates, 3-mile household count, drive-time population, your 14-factor scorecard, and the investor memo.

The updated page is on its card now — same three open questions as before (drive-time method, how to show intersection traffic, how sites get in). Say go ahead whenever you want it built.

checks.why: 'Car Wash Site Screener — Austin, full scorecard + investor memo' v1 is drafted: 5 steps: Receive site address (you); Screen the gates (alpha); Compute catchment (alpha); Score the 14 factors (both); Write the investor memo (alpha). Keeps sites, scorecard_factors, investor_memos. 2 suggestions: Use drive-time isochrones, not just a radius, for population; Cross-check your 14 factors against OPW's published checklist. Settings 5, questions 3.
